title: Applied ML Engineer
description_preview:
**Role Overview** 




  






 We are looking for an Applied Machine Learning Engineer to help build the model development, experimentation, evaluation, and deployment machinery for a new generation of proprietary analytical systems.
 




  






 This role sits at the intersection of applied machine learning, data engineering, mathematical modeling, and production software. You will work directly with technical leadership to translate proprietary mathematical and theoretical structures into practical ML workflows, model experiments, validation systems, and production\-ready inference tools.
 




  






 We need someone who can build production\-ready systems: feature pipelines, training workflows, evaluation harnesses, model comparison tools, inference services, and monitoring processes.
 





 We are moving fast. Multiple major initiatives have aggressive timelines, so we need someone who can contribute immediately and maintain a strong pace.
 




  





**Responsibilities** 




  




* Build applied ML pipelines for proprietary data, analytical features, and model targets.
* Work with technical leadership to translate mathematical concepts into computational representations.
* Design and implement feature engineering workflows, training datasets, model evaluation tools, and experiment tracking.
* Develop validation frameworks that prevent data leakage, overfitting, look\-ahead bias, and misleading performance claims.
* Train, compare, and evaluate multiple model families based on the structure of the problem.
* Build reproducible model training and inference workflows.
* Package successful models into production\-ready services, batch jobs, or internal tools.
* Collaborate with Python/data engineers to integrate ML workflows into larger data systems.
* Create model documentation, assumptions, limitations, and performance summaries.
* Help establish best practices for model versioning, monitoring, retraining, drift detection, and reproducibility.



  





**Required Qualifications** 




  




* Strong professional experience with Python and applied machine learning.
* Strong understanding of scikit\-learn, pandas, NumPy, and modern ML workflows.
* Experience building end\-to\-end ML pipelines from raw data through evaluation and deployment.
* Strong understanding of train/test splitting, validation design, leakage prevention, and model evaluation.
* Experience with time\-series, sequential, financial, operational, scientific, logistics, or similarly structured data.
* Ability to work with ambiguous, proprietary, or non\-standard problem definitions.
* Ability to think from first principles and build systems appropriate to the problem.
* Strong software engineering habits: modular code, testing, documentation, reproducibility, and clean interfaces.
* Comfort working closely with domain experts and translating mathematical intent into implementation.
* Clear communication about model behavior, limitations, risks, and tradeoffs.



  





**Preferred Qualifications** 




  




* Experience with PyTorch, XGBoost, LightGBM, statsmodels, MLflow, Databricks ML, or similar tooling.
* Experience with forecasting, classification, ranking, anomaly detection, representation learning, or sequence modeling.
* Experience with model deployment, batch inference, APIs, or production ML systems.
* Experience designing backtests, simulation frameworks, or historical validation systems.
* Familiarity with feature stores, model registries, experiment tracking, and monitoring.
* Experience working with proprietary algorithms, quantitative systems, or mathematically complex domains.
* Familiarity with Spark, Databricks, SQL, parquet, Delta tables, or large\-scale analytical workflows.



  





**What Success Looks Like** 




  






 Within the first 30 days, you understand the available data, help define initial modeling targets, build early feature and evaluation pipelines, and begin running controlled experiments.
 




  






 Within 60 days, you have helped establish a repeatable ML workflow that can ingest proprietary features, train candidate models, evaluate performance reliably, and support production deployment decisions.
 




  





**Ideal Candidate** 




  






 You ask what the system is actually trying to infer, what information is available at prediction time, how labels are constructed, where leakage might occur, and what failure would look like in production.
 




  






 You are practical, mathematically literate, implementation\-oriented, and comfortable building ML systems around proprietary domain logic that may not fit standard textbook examples.

**About You**
 You’re endlessly curious, adaptable, and detail\-obsessed in the best way. You love rolling up your sleeves to wrestle messy data into shape, making it clean, usable, and ready to reveal its secrets. You’re excited to learn from seasoned teammates but are also comfortable working independently on well\-defined problems from day one.
   

  

 You thrive in a collaborative, friendly, and nerdy environment where people genuinely love what they do. You chase the thrill of deep focus, appreciate your teammates’ brainpower, and hunger for the rush of solving problems no one else has dared to tackle. These are the kinds of challenges that stay with you—in the shower, as you fall asleep, tugging at your brain in the best possible way.
   

  

 You’re interested in politics, and the ways in which public opinion is created and shaped. You understand the power of narratives to shape the world around us, and want to play a part in the high\-stakes, real\-world battle over hearts and minds.
   

  

 Most importantly, you bring humility, patience, and a commitment to detail. You bring focus and efficiency to your work, knowing when to go deep and when to ship ‘good enough.’ You see this role as a chance to sharpen your craft, learn fast, and make a real contribution to high\-stakes, real\-world problems.
   

  

**About The Role**
 At Tavern Research, we’re building models to understand and influence how people form opinions online. That means taking on problems like tracing how narratives spread through social platforms, or analyzing how different messages land with different audiences. The data is messy, the questions are ambiguous, and the stakes are high.
   

  

 As a member of the Data Science team, your role is to help make this work possible. You’ll dive into raw, noisy datasets to clean, structure, and prepare them for analysis. You’ll run exploratory analyses to surface patterns, build features, and support experiments. You’ll contribute to modeling tasks end\-to\-end, helping turn difficult, open\-ended questions into tangible, testable results. While you’ll collaborate closely with senior modelers, we expect new hires to ramp quickly and take ownership of clearly scoped modeling and data tasks.
   

  

 From day one, you’ll be hands\-on with real\-world data and problems that matter. You’ll have support from senior team members, but you’ll also be expected to bring rigor, patience, and persistence to your work. Over time, as your skills deepen, you’ll have opportunities to take ownership of increasingly complex modeling projects, building toward the point where you can design and lead experiments yourself.
   

  

 We value in\-person collaboration and expect employees to work regularly from our Chicago office.
   

  

**Responsibilities**
* Work hands\-on with real\-world, unstructured data: cleaning, debugging, and engineering features that support effective models.
* Support the design and execution of numerical experiments by handling data prep, fitting models, and running standard analyses.
* Contribute to feature engineering and model building, taking ownership of clearly defined components of modeling projects.
* Write clean, well\-documented Python code using standard data science libraries.
* Assist with model evaluation, diagnostics, and performance monitoring.
* Collaborate with researchers and engineers to scope and execute tightly defined tasks.
* Learn and apply best practices and emerging tools in machine learning, AI, and causal inference.

* Strong academic or applied background in data science and software engineering or closely related fields.
* Experience building statistical models (beyond differential equations or simulations).
* Demonstrated experience working with messy, real\-world datasets.
* Proficiency in Python and standard data science libraries.
* Familiarity with AI and machine learning concepts like embeddings, supervised and unsupervised ML methods, and agentic systems
* Clear understanding of the data science concepts behind work you’ve done (not just “I ran the code”).
* Strong communication skills and a collaborative mindset
* Humility, patience, and attention to detail.
* We especially value candidates who have independently built data or modeling projects outside of coursework, including internships, research, or production data work.
* Bonus: exposure to model deployment, large language models, or causal inference.
